[RT-1] Unbatched high-rate publishes per client
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L260)
Evidence: The client publishes position and animation separately on a fixed 100ms interval (two publishData calls per tick), resulting in ~20 data packets/sec per client sent via LiveKit data channels. There is no batching, rate-limiting, or delta-compression in the publish path.  
Impact: With many participants the message rate multiplies (20 msg/s × N producers), causing network/CPU saturation on clients and LiveKit, high egress/billing and elevated packet loss/latency leading to dropped or delayed state.  
Fix: Bundle position+animation into a single message, lower send frequency, send only deltas when changed, and apply client-side rate limits or adaptive throttling.

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-1] Unbatched high-rate publishes per client
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L260)
Evidence: The client publishes position and animation separately on a fixed 100ms interval (two publishData calls per tick), resulting in ~20 data packets/sec per client sent via LiveKit data channels. There is no batching, rate-limiting, or delta-compression in the publish path.  
Impact: With many participants the message rate multiplies (20 msg/s × N producers), causing network/CPU saturation on clients and LiveKit, high egress/billing and elevated packet loss/latency leading to dropped or delayed state.  
Fix: Bundle position+animation into a single message, lower send frequency, send only deltas when changed, and apply client-side rate limits or adaptive throttling.

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-2] No ordering/sequence or replay for state updates
File: src/controller/RemotePlayersController.tsx (L1-L220)
Evidence: Incoming data is stored in plain maps and consumers require both position and animation maps to contain an identity before rendering; payloads have no sequence IDs/timestamps or ACK/replay logic. This makes the UI dependent on both channels arriving in-order and on-time.  
Impact: Packet loss, reordering, or delayed channels cause players to be missing, show stale or inconsistent state, or produce visible jitter under load or poor networks.  
Fix: Add monotonic sequence numbers or timestamps into published payloads, accept partial updates, and apply last-writer-wins + interpolation/replay logic to recover missed messages.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-3] No backpressure/drop policy for slow/blocked publishes
File: src/controller/NetcodeController.tsx (L1-L260)
Evidence: publishData is awaited and guarded by simple per-type locks (positionSendLock/animationSendLock) but there's no bounded queue, non-blocking enqueue, or policy to drop old/superceded messages if publish is slow.  
Impact: If LiveKit or network is slow, publishes can lag the 100ms cadence or be effectively dropped, causing missed updates and head-of-line blocking for subsequent sends.  
Fix: Use a bounded non-blocking send queue with drop-old policy or sample-replacement, avoid awaiting publishes on the main send timer, and expose adaptive backoff when publish latency grows.
